# PDFtoPDFocr

## Project

- Repository: https://github.com/doc-bricks/PDFtoPDFocr
- Project license: MIT (LICENSE)
- Current source line: 1.1.4 (version frozen)
- Python wheel: distribution metadata only; use the source checkout and requirements to run the desktop application.
- Main application: PDFtoPDFocr_2.py
- Export format: EXPORTFORMAT.md
- Security and data-handling notes: SECURITY.md, PRIVACY_POLICY.md
- Selected third-party license information: THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt
- Store listing draft: STORE_LISTING.md

## Summary

PDFtoPDFocr is a desktop application for turning scanned PDFs and images into searchable PDFs. The application uses PySide6 for its interface, Poppler through pdf2image for PDF rasterization, Tesseract through pytesseract for OCR, and pikepdf for PDF output.

The OCR and PDF-processing steps use local files and tools. The GUI source can request a missing Tesseract traineddata file from GitHub for the selected OCR language. This describes an application behavior; the program does not provide a firewall, network filter, or sandbox.

## Related projects

These are separately usable tools in the same project ecosystem; this list does not imply runtime integration:

- [DokuReader](https://github.com/doc-bricks/DokuReader) — local document-reading library.
- [UniversalDocsGrabber](https://github.com/doc-bricks/UniversalDocsGrabber) — retrieves document attachments from email workflows.
- [UniversalInvoiceMail](https://github.com/doc-bricks/UniversalInvoiceMail) — extracts invoice data and can export DATEV-style CSV; this is not a DATEV certification.

## Application data and network behavior

- Source documents are opened for local processing and output PDFs are written to the selected destination. The application does not provide a document-upload feature.
- When the selected Tesseract language data is missing, the GUI can make an HTTPS GET request to GitHub for that language data. This request is for the public model file, not the selected PDF.
- The UI language and export-folder preference are stored in a per-user configuration file under the platform configuration directory.
- An exported pdftopdfocr-job-v1.json manifest can include local paths, language, status, messages, and output hints. Review it before sharing; it does not embed the PDF bytes.
- The application does not restrict network access for the operating system or for other installed tools. Child processes inherit the launching process's permissions.

## Main components

- GUI, job queue, and worker: PDFtoPDFocr_2.py
- Translation tables and language switching: translations.json, translator.py
- Translation consistency checker: python manage_translations.py --check
- Job export format: EXPORTFORMAT.md
- Portable build workflow: build_release.py --clean
- PyInstaller specification: PDFtoPDFocr.spec

## Development commands

The project source supports Python 3.10 or newer. Install the dependencies listed in requirements.txt; development checks are listed in requirements-dev.txt.

- Run from a source checkout: python PDFtoPDFocr_2.py
- Check translations: python manage_translations.py --check
- Run tests: python -m pytest
- Check lint: python -m ruff check .
- Compile Python sources: python -m compileall -q .
- Build a local release bundle: python build_release.py --clean

pyproject.toml contains project and build metadata. Its metadata wheel is not a desktop application installer; use the documented source or Windows build path.

## Documentation languages

The README is available in English, German, Spanish, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and Russian. Detailed guides are linked from each language entrypoint.
